# Governance sync with Nadia Okonjo — both engagements

2026-05-11, 11:00 to 11:40, her office. First time either engagement has sat down with her rather than emailing.

Present: Adaeze Nwoye, Bridget Lomax, Tomas Kral, Nadia Okonjo.

We went in to ask two questions about two extracts and came out with the shape of the thing both engagements have been queuing behind since February.

The data-sharing review board is the gate for any member data leaving the system that holds it. Not a project step — a standing function, and it covers anything at Calderwood that moves member data, whether that is a Slalom team, an internal change, or a vendor. Nadia chairs it. It has five members drawn from claims, underwriting, actuarial, IT and the office of the Company Secretary, and none of them sit on it full time.

The rhythm, which is the part nobody had written down anywhere we could find:

It sits fortnightly, alternate Tuesdays. Papers close ten working days before the sitting. A request that misses the close waits for the next sitting, and Nadia was unambiguous that this does not flex: the members are borrowed from four business areas and the only thing that holds them to the date is that the date never moves. She has refused late papers for the finance system replacement and she said so in a tone that suggested she expected us to test it.

Worst case from "we know what we are asking for" to "we have an approval" is therefore about twenty-four working days, and that is with the paper right the first time. Nadia said roughly a third come back for rework, mostly because the purpose is written too broadly.

Two things about how the board reads a request, both of which change how we write ours:

It reviews the request, not the requester and not the programme. It has no visibility into delivery dates and does not accept them as an argument. Her line, which I wrote down as she said it: "Two programmes this year have told me their go-live was at risk. It is not an input. It is not that I do not care, it is that if it were an input I would have no basis for saying no to anyone."

And an approval is bounded on three axes — a named dataset, a named purpose, and twelve months. Reuse of an approved extract for a different purpose is a new request, not a variation, and she has turned down a variation on that basis before.

On where she sits: the board deliberately reports through the Company Secretary rather than through IT or through Operations. Nadia was explicit that this is the point of it — a governance function inside either side of the house would be leaned on by whichever programme was closest to a date. It is why the CIO cannot expedite for us and why an operations director cannot either, and both have been asked.

Practical consequences for us, which Bridget and Tomas both took away:

- Neither engagement can treat this as a step at the end. It is a twenty-four-day dependency at the front, and both plans currently have it nowhere.
- The purpose statement is the thing that gets rejected, so we write it narrow and we write it early.
- The twelve-month expiry means a pilot approval will lapse before a delivery programme built on it would finish, which is a conversation to have once rather than twice.

Actions:

- Adaeze to get both engagements onto the fortnightly calendar as a standing awareness item, not as a submission
- Bridget to draft the pre-prod masking paper for the sitting on the 26th, which means papers by the 12th, which means tomorrow
- Tomas to write the case-level purpose statement and have Nadia read it informally before it goes in — she offered, unprompted, and said most reworks would not happen if people did
